what_happened: A speech engine picks one pronunciation for each spelling. In one of our renders the past tense of a common verb came out with the present-tense sound, and a speech-to-text check could not catch it because it writes the same letters for either sound. We added a text check that runs before a render, and a marker that lets a lyric sheet state the spoken form of one word in braces. A person listened to a render that used the marker and confirmed the words came out as intended.
lesson: When one spelling has two sounds, say which one before the take: reword the line, or mark the spoken form. Do not rely on listening back by machine.

evidence.claim: A lyric sheet can write a word with its spoken form in braces; the linter, the gate and the renderer read the spoken form
The marker was first used in a render on 2026-11-14 and the owner confirmed by ear that the marked words came out as intended

redaction.method: by-value scan with verify.py: no credentials, hosts or addresses
